notes: Repairs for the six pre-V4 catalog entries that returned ZERO_RESULTS in the recheck of the original 50. Verify with --recheck: the six REPAIR candidates deliberately reuse the existing catalog id, so 'already in the catalog' must stop being an error. Every other rule still blocks. INTEGRATION RULE, so the outcome is deterministic: for each of the six entries, if its REPAIR verifies, replace that entry's coordinate/label in place and ignore the paired FALLBACK even if the fallback also verified; if the REPAIR fails and the FALLBACK verifies, delete the uncovered entry and add the fallback in the same commit; if both fail, change nothing and leave the entry exactly as it is. Catalog size is unchanged in all three outcomes. No panoId appears here: one may only come from a real verification run.

candidates.label: El Malecón, Havana
candidates.source: REPAIR. Original coordinate 23.1400/-82.3600 sits off the seawall in Centro Habana. Moved onto the Malecón roadway (Avenida de Maceo) in Vedado, opposite the Hotel Nacional — the widest named public road in the city.
candidates.rationale: Cuba is the one entry here where official car coverage is genuinely doubtful, so this is the only repair expected to fail. It is still worth one request: the Malecón is the single most likely covered road in the country, and the metadata endpoint accepts Google-hosted photospheres as well as car imagery (batch 005 resolved two that way). Stays hard/urban: a seafront road with Spanish signage and no skyline gives little away.

candidates.label: Half Way Tree Road, Kingston
candidates.source: FALLBACK for havana-malecon. Half Way Tree Road, the main north-south arterial through Kingston, well clear of the tourist coast.
candidates.rationale: Same difficulty, setting, continent and 'capitals' collection membership as the entry it would replace. Hard, not easy: an ordinary Caribbean commercial arterial with English signage, no landmark and no coastline — the player has climate and vehicle side to work from and little else. Jamaica has missed once before, on a rural road; a named capital-city arterial is a different proposition.

candidates.label: Sphinx entrance, Al Haram Street, Giza
candidates.source: REPAIR. Original coordinate 29.9765/31.1325 is on open sand inside the plateau. Moved 230 m east onto the paved terminus of Al Haram Street (Pyramids Road) at the Sphinx entrance in Nazlet El-Semman.
candidates.rationale: Preserves the identity exactly — the Sphinx and the Great Pyramid are both in view from the street, so it stays easy/landmark/famous rather than degrading into a generic Cairo street. Al Haram Street is a long, wide arterial, which also makes it forgiving of small coordinate error.

candidates.label: Monument de la Renaissance Africaine, Dakar
candidates.source: FALLBACK for cairo-giza. The access road below the Renaissance Monument on the Collines des Mamelles, Dakar. The first choice here was Black Star Square in Accra; the collision check found it 20 m from ghana-accra-independence-square, which returned ZERO_RESULTS in batch 004, so that precinct is already known to be uncovered.
candidates.rationale: Same difficulty, setting and continent as the Giza entry, in a country the catalog has already proven. A 50 m bronze monument on a hilltop is unmistakable enough to be a fair easy round without being a world landmark. It is 8 km from the existing Place de l'Indépendance entry — the same 25 km cluster, but only two groups in it, well under the limit of three.

candidates.label: Dock Road, V&A Waterfront, Cape Town
candidates.source: REPAIR. Original coordinate -33.9036/18.4200 lands in the harbour basin and the pedestrian precinct around it. Moved 550 m south onto Dock Road, the named public street serving the Waterfront.
candidates.rationale: Highest-confidence repair in this batch — South Africa is the most thoroughly proven country in the catalog and Dock Road is an ordinary through street. Identity is preserved (still the V&A Waterfront) and the tier is unchanged: harbour buildings and Table Mountain behind make it normal rather than hard, but it is not the postcard view.

candidates.label: Ahmadu Bello Way, Abuja
candidates.source: FALLBACK for capetown-waterfront. Ahmadu Bello Way, the main arterial through central Abuja.
candidates.rationale: Same difficulty, setting, continent and empty tag set. Normal rather than easy: a planned modern African capital with English signage and wide boulevards is readable but not identifiable on sight — no landmark is in frame. 700 km from the Lagos entry, so it opens a second Nigerian region.

candidates.label: Avenue Houmman El Fetouaki, Marrakech
candidates.source: REPAIR. Original coordinate 31.6258/-7.9891 is inside Jemaa el-Fnaa, which is pedestrian-only. Moved 350 m southwest onto Avenue Houmman El Fetouaki, the named public road running along the medina's western edge.
candidates.rationale: Keeps Marrakech and the medina wall in frame while sitting on a road a car can drive. The 'famous' tag is dropped deliberately: the square is famous, an avenue beside the ramparts is not, and instruction 6 rules out famous replacements for a hard entry. Stays hard — red pisé walls, Arabic and French signage, no monument.

candidates.label: Avenue Habib Bourguiba, Tunis
candidates.source: FALLBACK for marrakech-medina. Avenue Habib Bourguiba, the central boulevard of Tunis.
candidates.rationale: Same difficulty, setting and continent, and no famous landmark in view. Hard rather than normal: French colonial architecture with bilingual Arabic/French signage reads as North African without narrowing to a country or city. Tunisia has missed once, on a different kind of coordinate; a named central boulevard in the capital is the strongest coverage bet the country offers.

candidates.label: Na Phra Lan Road, Bangkok
candidates.source: REPAIR. Original coordinate 13.7500/100.4914 is inside the Grand Palace grounds, which no car reaches. Moved 200 m north onto Na Phra Lan Road, the public street along the palace's north wall.
candidates.rationale: The palace walls, gates and roofline are directly in view, so difficulty, setting and both tags survive intact. Thailand is proven four times over, and Na Phra Lan Road is a normal traffic street, so this is a high-confidence repair.

candidates.label: Lane Xang Avenue, Vientiane
candidates.source: FALLBACK for bangkok-grandpalace. Lane Xang Avenue approaching Patuxai, Vientiane.
candidates.rationale: Same difficulty, setting and continent, and it keeps the 'capitals' membership the Bangkok entry carried. 'famous' is dropped on purpose: Patuxai is a real monument but not globally recognisable, which is precisely why it suits normal — Lao script and a ceremonial boulevard identify the region without naming the city.

candidates.label: India Gate hexagon, New Delhi
candidates.source: REPAIR. Original coordinate 28.6129/77.2295 is on the lawns at the monument itself, and Kartavya Path was pedestrianised in 2022. Moved 340 m east onto the C-Hexagon, the ring road that circles India Gate.
candidates.rationale: India Gate stays in view from the ring road, so the tier and both tags are unchanged. India has had Street View only since 2022 and coverage follows major roads, which is exactly what the C-Hexagon is.

candidates.label: Independence Avenue, Colombo
candidates.source: FALLBACK for delhi-indiagate. Independence Avenue at Independence Memorial Hall, Colombo.
candidates.rationale: Same difficulty, setting and continent, keeping 'capitals' and dropping 'famous' — the hall is a national monument, not a global one, so it does not turn a normal round into an easy one. Sri Lanka is proven twice, and Colombo is 95 km from the Kandy entry and 190 km from Ella.
